title: Federated Identity

validation.research: Five primary sources verified. Microsoft Azure Architecture Center establishes the delegated user-authentication pattern. Current final NIST SP800-63C-4 publication confirmed July2025; it establishes IdP/RP trust, issuer-qualified federated identifiers and account responsibilities. NIST SP800-63B-4 section5 explicitly describes independent IdP/RP session termination and RP authority over reauthentication. OpenID Connect Core1.0 errata set2 sections3.1.3.7 and5.7 establish validation and stable issuer/subject identity, including changeable/non-unique email. RFC9700 establishes code-flow, PKCE, callback and browser-bound transaction protection. No existing exact canonical article found. Identity Federation is a broader-name alias; SSO is a possible experience, OIDC/SAML are protocols and OAuth alone is not user authentication.

example_limits: Sequential in-memory RP account/authorization simulation after a real trusted protocol verifier has accepted a login. Login construction is explicitly a fixture operation and can be performed without an IdP; it is not authentication, cryptographic assertion validation or an unforgeable capability. No JWT implementation, live IdP, browser redirects, session cookies, automatic email linking/provisioning, durable links/grants or concurrent consistency guarantee. Real deployment still needs complete protocol validation, expected issuer/audience/transaction binding, approved account linking, current local authorization, secure independent session lifecycles, deprovisioning and provider/key failure handling. Local grant revocation here affects the next modeled operation, not every IdP/RP session globally.
